purpose: Pins collector prefix, event precedence and immediate-claim contracts.
behavior: Collects 3 MiB raw output plus stderr without drops under a 4 MiB cap; overflow returns exactly the first 1000 bytes and identifies its stream.
Tests late bytes after end, a shorter within deadline, limit preserving the other stream in the same batch, and read failure preserving only earlier prefixes.
Pre-claim or pending loss must produce Io; an unpolled collection already owns the consumer and dropping it prevents reclaim.
contracts: Collection must never make output containing a hole look complete.
dependencies: io/collect.rs and queue state are exercised with OS pipes and deterministic bare queues.
failures_or_limits: No child process runs in this suite; timing and assertions remain unexecuted here.

purpose: Distinguishes optional attached backpressure from normal output dropping.
behavior: Writes 40 MiB into a held 16 MiB queue and requires the writer to remain pending, then verifies exact bytes and zero gaps after consumption.
end releases the held writer and resumes dropping; detach releases it and credits retained output to drops.
With no consumer claim, hold still uses the unattached budget and allows the writer to finish.
contracts: Backpressure must not make stop/end depend on consumer progress.
dependencies: io/queue::holds_back and condvar wake paths are exercised through actual pipes.
failures_or_limits: A 200 ms receive timeout is the explicit pending-writer observation, not proof of timing on every system.

purpose: Checks line splitting, UTF-8-safe piece limits, gap boundaries and abandoned-byte accounting.
behavior: Covers LF, CRLF split across reads, blank lines and unterminated final text.
A long multibyte line splits at 1048575 then 151426 bytes; an exactly 1 MiB line with split CRLF remains one piece.
Loss terminates partial text with replacement decoding and puts loss on the next or final empty line; dropping the view counts unpublished CRLF and partial bytes.
contracts: continues marks pieces only, and no line spans a gap.
dependencies: io/out::Lines is exercised with pipes and exact manually fed queue boundaries.
failures_or_limits: Assertions describe expected output shapes; no test was executed.

purpose: Supplies bounded real-pipe and bare-queue infrastructure for I/O unit tests.
behavior: child creates two real OS pipes and starts Pumps while feed writes from threads; bare permits exact accept/finish event ordering without reader threads.
Async and thread waits use 20 s failure bounds; after_first_poll and pending control future admission boundaries.
Compile-time send checks cover chunk/line next, collect, ended, stdin write and close futures.
contracts: The suite intentionally starts no child process; pipe writers play its output side.
dependencies: io::Pumps, Shared and Stdin are the tested implementation.
failures_or_limits: until polls observed state with 1 ms sleeps; it is bounded but differs from the repository preference for marker-only synchronization.

purpose: Exercises output budgets, ordered gaps, decoder reset, consumer ownership and bounded drain.
behavior: Unclaimed 50 MiB retains exactly 1 MiB and reports remaining loss on an empty final chunk; paused attached 20 MiB retains 16 MiB.
A paced 64 MiB stream is exact; split/invalid UTF-8 and byte mode are checked, including decoder reset at a gap.
Second or post-detach claims fail; EOF waits for all pipe holders, end permits late cleanup bytes but cuts at DRAIN, and view-held bytes count when dropped.
contracts: Terminal output uses Stream::Pty and stdout accounting.
dependencies: io/out.rs and queue/mod.rs are exercised via actual pipes and bare queues.
failures_or_limits: Paced lossless output depends on explicit acknowledgments limiting inflight bytes; it does not claim unlimited buffering.

purpose: Checks stdin call order, write backpressure, close, abandon and broken-pipe settlement.
behavior: Two 2 MiB writes must remain ordered and noninterleaved before trailing c; repeated close succeeds and later writes are Closed.
An 8 MiB write cannot resolve until the reader has consumed at least 7 MiB.

The abandon test requires the two submitted pending writes and a later write to return Closed, without synchronizing that either submitted write has become active in the worker. Broken pipe gives Closed, and drop after a completed last write delivers EOF.
contracts: in_order deliberately polls futures in queue order; write completion means OS acceptance, not application consumption.
dependencies: io/stdin::Writer is exercised with real anonymous pipes.
failures_or_limits: No actual child lifecycle or supervisor is involved; tests were not run.

purpose: Builds public child handles and binds tree lifetime to input/output ownership.
behavior: Child exposes root wait separately from whole-tree stop and inventory; output/lines share a single claim and write requires piped or terminal stdin.
Pipe spawn validates before cancellation check, then creates client child, pumps and optional hold, arming timeout and memory watchers.
PTY spawn starts its output reader before Go, then arms watchers; dropping Child sends an immediate detached kill and ends/abandons I/O.
contracts: Pty resize accepts 1..32767 cells; PipeChild close_stdin is idempotent.
Startup I/O failures initiate tree cleanup before returning an error.
dependencies: client supplies Spawned/Tree; io supplies pumps/writer; process life/deadline/memory own policy.
failures_or_limits: Drop and startup-failure kill are nonblocking requests, not synchronous confirmations of tree disappearance.

purpose: Enforces timeout/cancellation across root lifetime and surviving descendants.
behavior: Pre-cancelled commands fail after validation and before spawn; a library-runtime Alarm starts counting immediately at creation.
The first deadline/cancellation stops the tree with configured grace; cancellation wins when both futures are ready in the same poll.
After root and output finish, remaining pipe-free members enter a weak-reference linger state with one-second inventory checks; deadline races a pending List.
contracts: Root exit already observed retains its own reason despite later descendant cleanup.
dependencies: process/life.rs commits cause; client inventory identifies remaining members.
failures_or_limits: Inventory error ends enforcement just like lost supervisor; a recoverable incomplete inventory can therefore cease the linger watch. The same limitation is explicitly acknowledged in source.

purpose: Converts native root status plus first library action into public Exit.
behavior: Native code or signal is always preserved; Killed, Timeout, Aborted or MemoryExceeded may override only the reason.
Exit/Signal passed as a cause count as no library action.
Signal names cover shared termination signals and OS-specific Linux/BSD numbering, falling back to SIG<number>.
contracts: A child handling termination and exiting zero still has the committed non-Exit reason.
dependencies: process/life.rs determines the committed cause; client RootExit supplies native status.
failures_or_limits: Mapping assumes Linux versus BSD-style numbering for non-Linux Unix platforms.

evidence.quote:
let own = match (os, num) {
        ("linux", 7) => Some("SIGBUS"),
        ("linux", 10) => Some("SIGUSR1"),
        ("linux", 12) => Some("SIGUSR2"),
        ("linux", 16) => Some("SIGSTKFLT"),
        ("linux", 29) => Some("SIGIO"),
        ("linux", 30) => Some("SIGPWR"),
        ("linux", 31) => Some("SIGSYS"),
        ("linux", _) => None,
        (_, 7) => Some("SIGEMT"),
        (_, 10) => Some("SIGBUS"),
        (_, 12) => Some("SIGSYS"),
        (_, 30) => Some("SIGUSR1"),
        (_, 31) => Some("SIGUSR2"),
        _ => None,
    };
    shared.or(own).map_or_else(|| format!("SIG{num}"), str::to_owned)

purpose: Separates root result from tree stop and commits the first termination cause once.
behavior: Before first stop/kill, nonblocking unconstrained polling checks whether root exit is already known; known exit commits Root, otherwise commits the supplied library cause.
stop delegates whole-tree completion to Tree then returns the root status; kill sends zero-grace stop without waiting.
Converts process entries and validates grace by rounding nanoseconds up to milliseconds within u32 range.
contracts: Forked copies avoid locks and rely on client refusal; later causes never replace the first.
dependencies: client::Tree owns protocol lifecycle; process/exit.rs constructs Exit.
failures_or_limits: Cause is committed before sending termination; a later channel error is surfaced separately rather than undoing the cause.

purpose: Samples resident memory across tree members and descendant ancestry to enforce max_rss_bytes.
behavior: Every 250 ms obtains current tree members, then scans OS process memory on spawn_blocking, with Linux task duplication disabled.
Traverses descendants with a HashSet to avoid double counting multiple listed roots; missing sampled processes count zero.
RSS strictly above cap sends zero-grace MemoryExceeded and ends the watch; weak ownership releases on child drop.
contracts: Sampling expands beyond session membership, while stopping retains the supervisor tree boundary.
dependencies: sysinfo reports process parents and RSS; Life::processes supplies seed PIDs.
failures_or_limits: No hard allocation limit: short peaks may be missed; inventory/sample failure ends the watch. Escaped descendants are killed only through cooperating jail lifetime.

purpose: Defines process-layer exports and host-only launch defaults.
behavior: Exports Child/PipeChild/PtyChild and routes internal spawn/run functions to their modules.
Options hold cancellation, text mode, run input, output cap and pipe backpressure separately from validated spawn Request.
Defaults select text, no cancellation/input, 16 MiB per-stream max output and no backpressure.
contracts: Frozen seam covers handle methods, Options and launch entrypoints.
dependencies: api/command.rs populates Options; spawn::Request contains options requiring pure validation.
failures_or_limits: This module sets defaults but performs no spawn, memory sampling or timeout work.
